f_alters.title: Did you know?
f_alters.text: Alters are not separate people. They are parts of one whole person — each holding different roles, feelings, or memories that helped the person cope.

f_switching.title: Did you know?
f_switching.text: ‘Switching’ between alters is usually subtle — a shift in tone or posture — and is often a response to stress or a specific trigger, not a dramatic transformation.

f_origin.title: Did you know?
f_origin.text: DID typically develops in early childhood as a protective response to repeated overwhelming experiences. It is a sign of remarkable resilience, not danger.

f_coconscious.title: Did you know?
f_coconscious.text: Many people with DID experience ‘co-consciousness’ — alters can be aware of one another and cooperate, sharing thoughts in the background instead of switching fully.

f_treatment.title: Did you know?
f_treatment.text: DID is treatable. With safety and good therapy, alters can learn to cooperate, and many people reach a stable, fulfilling life. Integration is one possible goal — not a cure imposed from outside.

f_recovery.title: Did you know?
f_recovery.text: Healing from trauma rarely means forgetting. More often it's being able to tell the story — safely, in your own time, to someone who listens — until it no longer controls you.
